title: Deposit accounting in underlying units lets fair-rate depositor steal value from earlier discount-rate depositor

classification.assetImpact: Silent value transfer between depositors. A client depositing at a favourable AMM rate is credited with the same per-underlying principal as a client depositing at an unfavourable rate, even though the favourable depositor contributed more vault shares to the pool.
attackPath: 1. Client A deposits 1000 USDe when the Curve sUSDe/USDe pool is favourable: receives 1100 sUSDe shares for 1000 underlying.
3. Later Client B deposits 1000 USDe when the pool is unfavourable: receives 900 sUSDe shares for 1000 underlying.
5. On withdraw, the pro-rata formula totalShares * clientBalances / totalDeposited gives A and B identical shares despite A having contributed 22% more shares to the pool - A subsidises B.
classification.likelihood: high - the AMM rate fluctuates continuously and any deposit timing differential triggers the bug
classification.assumptions: multi-client model, routine AMM rate fluctuation

justification: Direct loss of client funds via the principal-tracking unit mismatch. The research doc only modeled vault.deposit() (deterministic shares) and never analysed the AMM-swap variant. Any honest client can be silently diluted by an unrelated client's lucky timing.
